findings.title: P11 leaves current publication summaries stale
findings.statement: The remote author branch is ed0ec0c, but unqualified remote-head summaries name 4bf2718; P11 has no successor entry in the audited tree.
evidence: Direct owner handoff confirms P10 and P11 separately
findings.consequence: Current publication-state wording is inaccurate; this is not a missing authorization or a scientific defect.
findings.suggested_resolution: Record P11 once in a chronological successor, with the direct current confirmation. Call P10 the last recorded publication event; put current remote head in a separately timestamped snapshot. Do not chase a self-referential push record.

findings.title: Strict JSON is not guaranteed transitively for genuine H records
findings.statement: Imported 1G-B configurations validate scalar values without storing native scalars. A valid H result can contain Fraction/NumPy fields whose export fails strict JSON.
evidence: implementation_scalar_probes_results.json: 1446 probes, 129 accepted exports fail strict JSON, zero imported-class behavior changes
12 genuine nested-H counterexamples: ten quadrature representations and two density/radius Fraction inputs
findings.consequence: The typed-float repair improves the intended H fields, but the universal export promise and assertion that imported records already store floats are false. Physical factory results are unchanged.
findings.suggested_resolution: Under an authorized follow-up, normalize supported nested scalar inputs or reject unsupported representations consistently, and test json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False) on nested H results. Until then narrow the documented guarantee; do not silently edit the frozen module.

findings.title: New tests miss float branches, a conversion and binding-tolerance drift
findings.statement: Phase tests and all evidence gates accept mutations that reject legitimate float subclasses, admit non-JSON float32 diagnostics, omit one scalar conversion, or increase the binding tolerance by 10%.
evidence: mutation_extra_results.json B01/B02/B03/B10 survive 49 phase tests and 36 gates
implementation_survivor_probes_results.json independently distinguishes all four from baseline
findings.consequence: The new tests close the specified earlier survivors but do not fully protect the advertised type/conversion and tolerance policy.
findings.suggested_resolution: Cover all five converted check fields and G, accepted numpy.float64/ordinary float subclasses, refused float32 outputs and nested exports. Pin RECORD_IDENTITY_RTOL independently if 1e-12 is policy. Tighten Monte Carlo/Simpson wording to their actual error budgets.

findings.title: Previously unseen validation gaps in frozen 1G-B result records
findings.statement: Unchanged LCDMReferenceLinearSigma accepts non-finite error diagnostics; AnchoredLagrangianSigmaRatio accepts arbitrary positive growth_ratio/early_spectrum_factor without binding their decomposition.
evidence: implementation_scalar_probes_results.json representative unbound.lcdm and unbound.anchor probes
lagrangian_sigma.py is byte-identical to 8d3cdd0; imported-class probes are unchanged against e517028
findings.consequence: Public direct result construction can export non-finite diagnostics or a misleading factor of 999. These two classes are not directly imported by H and no regenerated numerical result changes. This is new discovery in unchanged material, not a regression of GH-DF2.
findings.suggested_resolution: Authorize a narrowly scoped 1G-B contract-hardening successor: validate finite/domain-appropriate diagnostics and bind the factor decomposition or explicitly label those fields unverified metadata. Preserve frozen historical numerical records; make this follow-up scope decision explicit before promotion.

findings.title: CW minus one is not generally a literal both-walls conditional covariance
findings.statement: CW is explicitly E[psi1 psi2 | both walls]. Its excess over one is referenced to one-wall normalization, whereas a covariance conditioned on both walls subtracts two both-conditioned means.
evidence: Independent Gaussian tilting derivation in science_comparison.md; law II shifts both-conditioned means away from one
findings.consequence: The formulas and computed statistic are correct; the exported covariance label can suggest a different centering.
findings.suggested_resolution: Explain CW−1 as a both-walls conditional product-moment excess relative to the one-wall mean, and distinguish it from the centered both-walls covariance. Preserve or deprecate any key with an explicit compatibility note rather than changing the science.

errata_of_third_remediation.quote: Fail-closed, and strict JSON holds by construction
errata_of_third_remediation.correct_reading: Named H recomputed float fields are finite and typed; named H scalar inputs are converted. Nested imported records still admit non-JSON scalars. The guarantee is incomplete (GH-D3F2).

errata_of_third_remediation.quote: The 1G-B records the runtime imports already store floats and are unchanged.
errata_of_third_remediation.correct_reading: They are unchanged, but not every validated field stores a native float; imported quadrature, density and radius inputs give nested H counterexamples.

errata_of_third_remediation.quote: an equal ``Fraction`` or ``int`` would pass the comparison but break the strict-JSON contract of ``to_json_dict``
errata_of_third_remediation.correct_reading: A Python int is valid strict JSON. Refusing integer substitutes is the declared typed-float output policy; Fraction/non-native scalar export failure is a different rationale.
